interest: Tracks Prince Masahito's 1935 birth and Prince Chichibu's 1937 coronation trip through Canada.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.0011/96 through 894.0011/99) covers diplomatic correspondence and cross-reference records concerning the Japanese Imperial Family between November 1935 and October 1937. It begins with a November 1935 telegram from the American Embassy in Tokyo announcing the birth of an imperial prince (Prince Masahito, later Prince Hitachi) to Empress Nagako. The subsequent records focus on Emperor Hirohito's younger brother, Prince Chichibu (Yasuhito), and Princess Chichibu (Setsuko) during their 1937 journey to and from the Coronation of King George VI in London. Through cross-reference sheets and attached reporting extracts from U.S. Minister to Canada Norman Armour, the file documents the Imperial couple's official stop in Ottawa in May 1937, correspondence concerning a proposed visit to the United States, and their return journey across Canada in September and October 1937, including their reception in Quebec by Canadian dignitaries such as Minister of Justice Ernest Lapointe and their train travel westward via Montreal and Niagara Falls toward the Pacific coast.
